attribution.notice: The upstream shared library read for this entry is authored by McJty and published under the MIT licence. It was read at the pinned revision below to write a behaviour specification. Ravel's counterpart is an independent implementation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or derived from the original's source text.

publication.notes: The fetched source lives only in the public repository's ignored fixture tree at tests/fixtures/local/m6-clean-room/ and is not tracked in either repository. The specification derived from it is tracked at specifications/m6-foundation/RVL-120.md and is not in the public repository. Neither is publishable while the names surface is unresolved. The fetched tree carries five binary images and one image source file: one interface texture in the shipped resources, four interface textures belonging to a demonstration source set that is not part of the shipped artifact, and one layered source image at the repository root. None was opened or read as behaviour and nothing is shipped from them. The tree carries no sound file and no model document.
publication.reviewedBy: structure-reviewed 2026-09-05 by an independent Claude reader that had seen no upstream source; it read the specification first and then the counterpart's module list and public types to see whether a structural noun had crossed, after the counterpart was implemented; verdict: accepted with findings, 1 finding fixed in the specification and the counterpart on 2026-09-05; the specification's read/inferred/unknown markers and closing coverage statement were checked present. No human has read the specification in full.

rights.basis: MIT, read at the source rather than trusted from the inventory. Reading, modification and derivative works are permitted, which is what source-informed reimplementation requires. The counterpart must not copy source text; the specification written from this read carries no upstream identifier, which checks/verify-spec-identifiers.sh was run over and returned no finding. Three serialised spellings the original writes into saved data are deliberately not transcribed either: the specification states the behaviour and marks the spellings unknown to it, so a counterpart that needs save compatibility reads them from the pinned artifact at build time rather than from a document this record clears.
MIT imposes no behavioural restriction and the inventory records behaviour as cleared and sourceUse as permitted for this entry.

Unchanged from the inventory. MIT does not grant trademark rights, so the project's own name, its mod id and its content identifiers remain unresolved. The specification therefore names nothing after the original, and no save-compatible identifier mapping is specified. The constraint bites in one specific place for this entry: it registers seven item data component kinds and two data attachments whose identifiers are the vocabulary its dependents store on their own items, so a counterpart that is save-compatible with the original is exactly what this record cannot clear.

One interface texture ships with the entry and four more belong to a demonstration source set that is not part of the shipped artifact; a layered source image sits at the repository root. None was fetched for reading and none was read. The inventory records textures as cleared for this artifact and the licence reserves no asset separately. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped; any counterpart art is rewritten from reference under policies/source-access.json and recorded in the package's assets-provenance.json.

The fetched tree contains no model document. Its one block-state document names a model for a block that is not registered at this revision, and that document was read as a registration census entry rather than as an asset. The inventory records models as not-applicable for this artifact.
The fetched tree contains no sound file, which is what the inventory's not-applicable verdict for this artifact holds. The specification refers to no sound.

No branding material was fetched or read; the display name, logo and author identity are excluded regardless of licence status under policies/source-access.json. The mod descriptor was read only to confirm the dependency, side and licence declarations the specification's sections 1 and 2 state, and none of that text is transcribed.

sources.use: The upstream implementation, fetched as a source archive into the public repository's ignored fixture tree at tests/fixtures/local/m6-clean-room/tar/ and extracted alongside it, and read to write specifications/m6-foundation/RVL-120.md. Version correspondence to the pinned pack artifact -- exact: the build script at this revision declares version '1.21-9.0.20' and an archive base name that together produce the pinned artifact file name mcjtylib-1.21-9.0.20.jar, and it declares the toolchain and loader range the artifact was built against. The revision was located by reading the build-script history on the branch the project keeps for this game version: the upstream project publishes no tag and no release, and names one branch per game version, so the branch is unambiguous and the version is declared in a properties file rather than a tag. This commit is the one that declared the pinned version, and its message says so. Four later commits on the same branch still declare that version before the bump to the next one; they are post-release development, the last of them an unfinished port of one subsystem, and none was read. No decompilation was performed and no jar was opened.

sources.use: The licence, verified at the source rather than trusted from M5's triage. It is the MIT licence verbatim, twenty-one lines, carrying the standard permission grant with no additional term and no separate asset reservation. Its copyright line names the year 2016 and no holder, which is a defect in the notice rather than in the grant: the grant itself is unconditional and the project's mod descriptor in the same tree declares the licence as MIT and points at this file. MIT permits reading, modification and derivative works, so the inventory's permitted verdict for this entry is confirmed rather than assumed. A counterpart that reproduced any of this text would owe the notice a named holder, which is one more reason nothing here is copied.

sources.revision: as frozen by M5 and consumed by the foundation wave manifest
sources.use: The claims this record checks: the entry is sourceUse permitted with method source-informed-reimplementation, owner sdk-platform, artifact mcjtylib-1.21-9.0.20.jar, no dependency on any other inventory entry, and a declared MIT licence with assets not reserved separately. All confirmed above; the absent dependency is confirmed against the mod descriptor, which declares the loader as its only requirement. The wave manifest admits the entry as a foundation seed, and the plan rows record RVL-025 inside this wave and RVL-018, RVL-051, RVL-200 and RVL-293 outside it as the entries that depend on it, which is what the specification's section 16 is written against. One inventory-adjacent claim is qualified rather than confirmed: the plan row assigns the entry the recipe-free test set it in fact needs, and this read found the entry ships no recipe, tag, loot or world-generation document at all, so three of its dependents' parity tests can only be about their own content.

sources.use: Records the fetch. No fetch tool exists in either repository; the earlier rows were written by hand and this one was fetched with a plain archive download from the same host and appended in the same form, digesting the archive with sha256 as the existing rows do. The digest binds the archive as fetched at the time above rather than asserting that the host re-serves identical bytes. This repository had no pre-existing row, so nothing in the file competes with this one.
